answers.answer: Use the canonical package router `indexer-envio/AGENTS.md` together with the canonical package reference `indexer-envio/README.md`. The router identifies the hosted/testnet YAML configs, `schema.graphql`, required `src/EventHandlers.ts` entry point, vendored ABI generator, codegen command, and checked-in shared-config mirrors used by out-of-workspace hosted builds. The README owns the step-by-step contract-add procedure: update every applicable multichain config, generate or minimally vendor the ABI, update the schema, add the handler and side-effect import it from `src/EventHandlers.ts`, then run package codegen and the cross-layer checklist. For a new contracts deployment or namespace, it also says to update both the shared-config and indexer `deployment-namespaces.json` mirrors, regenerate ABIs, check YAML addresses, run codegen, and run the selected typechecks.

evidence.supports: The package router sends contract-add and promotion work to the README and names production config plus the loaded handler graph as operating truth.
The package router identifies the config, schema, required handler entry point, hosted-build mirrors, ABI directory, and ABI generator.
Schema, config, entry-point, or handler-reachability changes require indexer codegen.
Published ABIs and addresses come from the contracts package, while hosted builds require synchronized checked-in shared-config mirrors because they may run outside the workspace.
Codegen must use package scripts, and every new handler module must be imported through `src/EventHandlers.ts` before codegen.
The contracts-deployment promotion procedure updates both deployment-namespace mirrors, regenerates ABIs, checks YAML addresses, runs codegen, and runs typechecks.
The complete contract-add procedure covers ABI sourcing, all applicable multichain configs, schema entities, handler location and entry-point import, codegen, and the cross-layer checklist.
